about: Definition of the multi-frame enabler-free Intel-free variant (how it works: packaging/public/ARCHITECTURE.md; the C side: src/game/mfg_proxy.c with XEFG_PROXY_MFG and src/game/mfg_proxy_coexist.h): the libxess_fg.dll proxy of release/intel_free_2x.json, but with the multi-frame support of the enabler-era Intel-free add-on (release/intel_free.json) kept, so Intel's runtime gets this project's replacement pipelines at whatever frame count it runs: 2x on its own, and 3x/4x when another module the user installed has lifted Intel's frame limit for GPUs other than its own. FreeFG lifts no limit and patches nothing in Intel's runtime. When another module has hooked Intel's entry points, the lifecycle entries tail-call Intel's (that module sees the caller it would see without this proxy), contexts this proxy does not accelerate get the caller's own device and queue, and a model census or order of work this project did not verify makes the context step aside (Intel's or that module's shaders) instead of ending the game. Read by release/build_proxy.py --variant intel-free-mfg and release/assemble.py --variant intel-free-mfg.
configuration: Enabler-free Intel-free add-on, multi-frame: libxess_fg.dll proxy over Intel's unmodified XeFG runtime (bc250_xefg_original.dll), own shaders only, at the frame count the runtime runs (multi-frame network, pooled model sets, retirement at frame-count changes, SDK-status pacing signal); beside another module hooking the runtime it keeps the callers of the lifecycle entries and steps aside instead of ending the game; no XeSSMFG enabler or MinHook; the bundled OptiScaler supplies adaptive frame-start correction at 3x/4x

dropped_defines.XEFG_MFG_XELL_PACE=1: The old frame-start pacer reads the enabler's ApplyMultiplier hook and inline-hooks XeLL and the SDK's Present. This proxy hooks neither. MFG Unlocker's output pacing does not correct game simulation starts; the OptiScaler fork calls the adaptive controller directly through its XeLL output at 3x/4x. The presentation layer still learns when XeFG generates (accelerated counters and the SDK's present status).
dropped_defines.XEFG_MFG_NO_ENABLER_UI=1: Hook on the enabler's overlay; no enabler.

kept_defines.XEFG_MFG_RESEARCH=1: Multi-frame network and its model census (the 2x, multi-frame or both model sets; mfg-finish kernels; late model sets).
kept_defines.XEFG_MFG_POOL=1: Pooled model sets and pipelines for the sets and pipelines Intel's runtime recreates at a frame-count change.
kept_defines.XEFG_MFG_RETIRE=1: Heap and list retirement after a frame-count change (xefgSwapChainSetNumInterpolatedFrames), instead of the enabler's ApplyMultiplier.
kept_defines.XEFG_FRAME_CAP_RESEARCH=1: Generated-frame output tracking, owned resampling and retirement of released output resources.
kept_defines.XEFG_FLOW_CAP_RESEARCH=1: Generated-frame geometry tracking and reduction, enabled only when requested in settings.

added_defines.XEFG_F4Q=1: F4Q (FreeFG 1.1): this project's FP32 Winograd F(4x4,3x3) kernels for the U-Net decoder b3941ac8 and encoder f030948d in place of its F(2x2) kernels, on by default (src/model_f4q.h, src/game/f4q.h; profile "add"); since 1.1.2 also F4Q2, the same arithmetic for the encoders 1a3b0782, e83e868f and 9e0080ee, on by default while F4Q is on, and F4Q3, the same arithmetic for the row layers 60edebbb and b3ddf030 in place of their 1D kernel. Their outputs matched the F(2x2) and 1D kernels' in every test, which does not prove every input. Also since 1.1.2 the FP16 forms, on by default while F4Q is on: seven U-Net kernels in faster forms whose outputs differ slightly from the exact forms' (and so from Intel's): FP16 coefficient tables in the three F4Q2 kernels and packed-FP16 MACs in four F(2x2) kernels, read from <hash>.fp16.dxil with FP16 copies the model owner adds; F4Q's two kernels and F4Q3 run in their exact forms. BC250_XEFG_F4Q=0, or F4Q=0 in BC250-XeFG/settings.ini, turns all of them off; BC250_XEFG_F4Q2=0, or F4Q2=0, turns F4Q2 off alone; BC250_XEFG_EXACT=1, or Exact=1, turns the FP16 forms off (every kernel exact; the output identical to Intel's in every test); BC250_XEFG_F4Q_SHADOW=1 is a diagnostic that runs the F4Q, F4Q2 and F4Q3 kernels beside the F(2x2) and 1D kernels and counts equal and differing outputs on the GPU.
added_defines.XEFG_REF64_GX16=1: FreeFG 1.1.2: the fused flow refinement (src/winograd_graph.h) dispatches its wino-ref64 kernels over the output size in 32 x 4 px groups; the profile's wino-ref64-16/17/18.dxil are the release recipes with GX=16 and ACC_SHR=1 (profile "replace"). Both changes are exact: the same outputs for every input the model owner accepts.
added_defines.XEFG_OWN_FRAME_SCALING=1: FreeFG-owned colour resampling around original SDK pipelines; reduced generation geometry.
added_defines.XEFG_MFG_UP_FILTERS=1: Owned bilinear, bicubic, Lanczos2 and AMD FSR 1 EASU enlargement of generated frames.
added_defines.XEFG_SCALE_DIRECT_OUTPUT=1: Write reduced synthesis directly into the enlargement input.
added_defines.XEFG_SCALE_COPY_REUSE=1: Reuse reduced SDK copy histories until a later write or abandoned list invalidates them.
added_defines.XEFG_SCALE_OUTPUT_RT_LAYOUT=1: Allow lossless render-target compression of supported enlargement-input allocations.
added_defines.XEFG_SCALE_RT_LAYOUT=1: Allow lossless render-target compression of supported reduced-colour allocations.

profile.name: cl-wino-q33-intel-free-mfg
profile.replace_about: Files of the Intel-free profile this build ships in another form of this project's own, from the inputs.lock.json tree group "own_files" (release/profile-mfg; recipes in its origin.json, rebuilt by release/build_profile.py check): the file takes the new bytes, and its waves.txt line (the same wave size) names the new module in place of the old one, so the table keeps its length and order (release/build_proxy.py prepare_profile). XU-1 (FreeFG 1.1): the nine U-Net shaders of wino_rs16.hlsl, wino_enc16.hlsl and wino_dec16.hlsl compiled with XU1=1 and -enable-16bit-types (the input transform in FP16 pairs, exact for the transform's small integers; in wino_rs16 also a wave-uniform epilogue). The FP32 products and sums are the release recipe's, so the outputs are the same: each kernel checked on the CPU (DXIL, lavapipe), and the generated images identical on all 20 SDK test rows on the BC-250 (2026-10-20). The two wino_row16 shaders keep their release recipe (XU1 measured slower there). The fused refinement (FreeFG 1.1.2, XEFG_REF64_GX16): wino-ref64-16/17/18.dxil compiled with GX=16 and ACC_SHR=1 (32 x 4 px groups, acc >> 2), both exact, so the outputs are the release recipe's for every input the model owner accepts; the proxy dispatches it over the output size. Their waves.txt lines name the new modules in place. release/profile itself, which the 2x build (0.9.0) and the enabler-era Intel-free add-on read, is not changed.

replace.wino-ref64-17.dxil: 1.1.2: wino_ref64.hlsl with GX=16 and ACC_SHR=1, clamp 17
replace.wino-ref64-18.dxil: 1.1.2: wino_ref64.hlsl with GX=16 and ACC_SHR=1, clamp 18

profile.add_about: Files of this project's own this build ships beside the Intel-free profile, from the same tree group (release/profile-mfg), with a waves.txt line appended after the append_waves lines when they have a wave size. F4Q (FreeFG 1.1, XEFG_F4Q): the FP32 Winograd F(4x4,3x3) kernels the proxy loads in place of the F(2x2) <hash>.dxil of b3941ac8 and f030948d while F4Q is on (src/game/f4q.h), and the check kernels of its diagnostic (BC250_XEFG_F4Q_SHADOW=1). The F(4x4) kernels are byte-identical to the ones round 3 tested: 20 of 20 SDK test rows identical, 96,480 in-game comparisons with 0 differing (Cyberpunk 2077, native 2x and OptiScaler 3x), 0.19-0.28 ms less GPU time per generated frame than the F(2x2) kernels on those two pipelines. F4Q2 (FreeFG 1.1.2, the same define): the same F(4x4) arithmetic for the encoders 1a3b0782, e83e868f and 9e0080ee (f4q_enc16.hlsl, one FP32 channel chain over all input slices), byte-identical to the kernels a test build ran on the BC-250 on 2026-10-23: 640 of 640 SDK frames identical on 19 test rows, 162,992 in-game comparisons with 0 differing (Cyberpunk 2077, native 2x and OptiScaler 3x), and in that test build 0.097 ms (SDR) and 0.142-0.146 ms (HDR10) less GPU time per generated frame than the F(2x2) kernels on those three pipelines. Identical in every test, not proven for every input. F4Q3 (FreeFG 1.1.2): the same F(4x4) arithmetic for the row layers 60edebbb and b3ddf030 (f4q_enc16.hlsl POOL=0), on by default while F4Q is on; identical in every test, not proven for every input. F4Q's two kernels are, since 1.1.2, their XU2D=1 TRIM=1 / TRIM=1 forms (exact: the same outputs). The FP16 forms (FreeFG 1.1.2, on by default): <hash>.fp16.dxil for seven U-Net pipelines (HALF_TABLE=1: FP16 coefficient pairs in the three F4Q2 kernels; PK16=1: packed-FP16 MACs in four F(2x2) kernels); their outputs differ slightly from the exact forms' and so from Intel's; BC250_XEFG_EXACT=1 or Exact=1 turns them off.

graph-prepare224.dxil.about: FreeFG 1.1.3.1: use wave64 for the 224-channel, 48-column input transform. On Cyberpunk 2077 2.5 with HelixSR Quality, BC-250, Mesa 26.2.5 and GE-Proton11-11, a wave-table bisection isolated this shader's wave32 selection as the trigger for an early GPU fault. The full table with only this choice changed runs; shader bytes and arithmetic are unchanged.

profile.append_dispatch_scale_about: Rows appended to the profile's dispatch-scale.txt (release/build_proxy.py prepare_profile): identity rows for the two U-Net row layers, so the dispatch hook sees their dispatches and gives a dispatch bound to an F4Q3 pipeline its F(4x4) groups (src/game/f4q.h). An identity row changes no other dispatch.
profile.append_waves_about: Lines appended to the profile's waves.txt (release/build_proxy.py prepare_profile; release/profile/waves.txt itself stays the pinned table, whose bytes remain the prefix): wave 32 for five of Intel's unchanged pipelines that run in this build where the full profile had Intel-derived replacements (release/INTEL-FREE.md), so their wave size was never chosen. The pacing layer requests it from the driver by module hash on the BC-250 only; the shader code is not changed. Measured 2026-10-20 on the BC-250: generated images identical on all 20 SDK test rows (SDR and HDR10, engine and pixel motion vectors, 1440p and 4K), 0.07-0.08 ms less GPU time per generated frame in SDR and 0.18 ms in HDR10. The pacing layer then reads 128 entries; one malformed or repeated line would make it drop the whole table, which prepare_profile refuses. The 2x variant (0.9.0) and the enabler-era Intel-free add-on keep the pinned table, so their reference builds stay reproducible.
